correctness.rationale: For \(A=\operatorname{diag}(a_1,\ldots,a_n)\) with positive distinct modes, the finite kernel \(C=VV^{\mathsf T}\) is strictly totally positive by generalized Vandermonde determinants and Cauchy–Binet, so \(H=EC^{-1}E\) is symmetric positive definite and strictly positive entrywise. All sensor phases cancel by unitary congruence. For a positive unit amplitude vector \(d\), the inverse Gram spectral radius is at least \(d^{\mathsf T}D^{-1}HD^{-1}d=\boldsymbol 1^{\mathsf T}H\boldsymbol 1=L\). Setting \(d_i^2=(H\boldsymbol1)_i/L\) makes \(D^{-1}HD^{-1}d=Ld\); the Perron–Frobenius theorem identifies \(L\) as the largest eigenvalue. Equality in the Rayleigh quotient forces \(d_i^2=r_i/L\). Rank-deficient boundaries are treated separately. The exact rational checker passes 885 assertions, including principal-minor positive-semidefinite certificates and the explicit three-mode example.

value.rationale: For an evolving diagonal state measured by a single unit-energy sensor, \(\lambda_{\min}\) controls the worst-direction inverse noise amplification. The result solves a natural exact E-optimal frame design problem in arbitrary dimension and all finite observable horizons, with a unique allocation and rational computable formula. This does not follow from D-optimality or condition-number minimization. The three-mode example demonstrates genuinely nonuniform weights and a sharp finite-horizon bound.
